evals.prompt: Here's a grep hit from our secrets scan on the inventory backend. Write it up as a proper audit finding and add it to audit/findings/audit-secrets-and-config.json. The line is in evals/files/raw-grep-line.txt.
evals.expected_output: One finding in the standard block (Title, Severity, Location, Evidence, Impact, Remediation, Reference) rated Critical, with a .NET-idiomatic remediation (configuration/secret store + rotation + history purge), CWE-798 referenced, appended to findings.json with the SEC prefix.
expectations: Output contains a finding whose severity is Critical
Location references appsettings.Production.json with a line number
Remediation mentions rotating the key and moving it to environment/secret store
Impact text does not contain the strings 'CWE' or 'IDOR' (plain language)

evals.prompt: quick one: the orders list endpoint in evals/files/sample-repo/src/orders/orders.controller.ts returns everything with no paging. can you write that up as a finding for the API audit? note is in evals/files/note.txt
evals.expected_output: One finding rated Medium (availability impact, authenticated precondition), API- prefix, location pointing at the listOrders handler, node/TypeScript remediation with take/skip and a pageSize cap, CWE-770 or ASVS 12.1.1 referenced, plus a one-line severity justification in Impact.
expectations: Output contains a finding whose severity is Medium
Location file is src/orders/orders.controller.ts with the listOrders line
Remediation mentions pagination parameters and a maximum page size
Impact contains a justification for the severity rating

evals.prompt: I have two findings in evals/files/dupes.json that are really the same bug (missing tenant filter in the base repository). Merge them into one finding and keep both locations.
evals.expected_output: A single merged finding with both file locations preserved in Evidence/extra.locations, the higher severity kept, references unioned, produced via python ../audit-findings-rollup/scripts/findings_rollup.py dedupe evals/files/dupes.json (preview, then --write on a copy) or equivalent.
expectations: Resulting findings array has exactly one entry
Merged finding lists both original locations
Both original ids are recorded in extra.merged_ids
